column1: # Every line maps something observable on the wire to something we can conclude
# about the device that emitted it. This file is plain data on purpose: the
# person who knows that a Zebra label printer announces itself a particular way
# is rarely a Go programmer, and requiring a code change to record that fact is
# the reason no open dataset of this kind exists today.
#   table       which signal this rule applies to (see the sections below)
#   match       a lowercase substring; the rule fires if the observed value contains it
#   weight      0..1, how much this observation is worth ON ITS OWN
#   spec        specificity. 1 is normal. Use 2 for a conclusion that refines a
#               vaguer one ("Windows 7" over "Windows") so the precise answer
#               wins even against a higher-weighted generic signal.
#   0.9  the device effectively announced what it is
#   0.5  a good indicator with known false positives
#   0.3  suggestive only, meant to combine with others
# Keep weights honest. Several weak signals combine as noisy-OR, so a signal
# scored as proof when it is merely suggestive does not just mislead on its own
# line — it drags every device sharing that signal toward false certainty.
# PROVENANCE RULE, and it is not optional:
# Entries must be derived from your own observations, vendor documentation, or
# other public-domain sources. Do NOT copy rows out of Fingerbank. Their data is
# licensed ODbL, which is share-alike: anything derived from it must also be
# ODbL, and that would silently destroy the CC0 licence this file carries.
# vendor_class: hardware vendor (usually from the MAC OUI) implies a class
# dhcp_vendor_class: DHCP option 60, the single best passive signal available.
# The device states what it is, unprompted, the moment it joins the network.
# Vendor class strings that also imply a class (or a vendor, where the primary
# Version-specific operating systems are spec 2 — an out-of-support Windows box
# is one of the most useful things this tool can surface, and it must not be
# masked by a generic "Windows" from a DHCP vendor class.
# ssh_banner: SSH version strings, from either side of the connection
# server_banner: HTTP Server headers, FTP banners, SNMP sysDescr
# Embedded devices are far more honest in their banners than general-purpose
# operating systems, which makes this a strong signal for exactly the devices
